stories.title: Dallas Multifamily 2026 Panelists Cautious, Hopeful About Industry Future
stories.excerpt: With so much competition, its doing the little things right that seemed to be a prevailing theme among several panelists at the recent Connect Texas Multifamily Dallas event at the Joule. John Tullo, from Apartment Management Consultants, said in a competitive market like Dallas, which has an 89% occupancy rate and a number of desirable amenities, it all boils down to execution: “You’re not winning on countertops or location, because there are plenty of good options. If you’re missing your mark on anything that is controllable, they’re moving across the street. Are you responding to leads? Are you doing anything to differentiate your product? Those are the things you can control.” Red Oak’s Gary Bechtel weighed in, noting that people are moving to Texas in droves. “There is a lot of overbuilding. It’s had a negative impact on rates and absorption. It gonna take a couple of years to work its way out. A lot of developers are looking outside the big cities, like College Station and El Paso.” Affinius Capital’s Hailey Ghalib stated, “There appears to be near-term operational pressure from the wave of supply that we’re continuing to work through, but it’s improving.” The post Dallas Multifamily 2026 Panelists Cautious, Hopeful About Industry Future appeared first on Connect CRE.
bullets: Dallas multifamily at 89% occupancy; panelists cite overbuilding, near-term operational pressure
Developers pivoting to secondary markets: College Station, El Paso as relief valve
Competitive differentiation shifting from product to execution and resident experience
stories.summary: Dallas multifamily market is saturated with new supply, driving 89% occupancy and pressure on rents and absorption. Panelists from Red Oak, Affinius Capital, and AMC noted that absorption will take years to normalize. In response, developers are moving away from trophy submarkets and looking at secondary Texas cities like College Station and El Paso to avoid direct competition.
stories.impact: Overbuilding in Dallas-Fort Worth core submarkets is compressing returns and forcing capital reallocation. Developers should monitor secondary Texas metros for earlier mover advantage before capital follows. Expect continued rent pressure in urban Dallas through 2026-27; suburban and secondary-market opportunities present higher upside in near term.

stories.title: Midtown Office Tower Scores Leases Totaling 182K SF
stories.excerpt: A trio of companies have inked leases totaling more than 182,000 square feet at The Swig Company’s 1411 Broadway following a $100 million renovation of the Midtown office tower. Software company Zeta Global signed a 10-year, 50,500-square-foot lease across the entire 38th and 39th floors of the property, doubling its footprint and relocating its headquarters, the New York Business Journal reported. Amorepacific, a South Korean beauty and cosmetics group, also committed to a 10-year, 50,500-square-foot lease at the tower. The company is moving its headquarters from 1407 Broadway. Rounding out the recent deals is Republic Clothing Corp., a current subtenant at the building, which agreed to a 15-year direct lease for 81,000 square feet across the three floors. CBRE represented ownership in the lease transactions. With a flurry of leasing activity over the past 18 months, occupancy at 1411 Broadway is expected to reach 90% by year-end. The Swig Company’s capital improvement program for the building has included a new entrance and facade, a renovated Broadway plaza, and other enhancements. A new rooftop amenity space is slated to open in early 2028. The post Midtown Office Tower Scores Leases Totaling 182K SF appeared first on Connect CRE.
bullets: Zeta Global HQ relocation to 1411 Broadway, 50.5K SF, 10-year lease
Tower leasing 182K SF across three tenants post-$100M renovation; 90% occupancy by year-end
Manhattan Midtown office-to-residential conversion risk diminishing; flight-to-quality capital evident
stories.summary: 1411 Broadway in Midtown Manhattan has leased 182,000 square feet following a $100 million capital improvement program. Anchor tenant Zeta Global relocated its HQ there (50,500 SF), joined by Amorepacific (50,500 SF HQ move from nearby 1407 Broadway) and Republic Clothing (81,000 SF). Occupancy is expected to reach 90% by year-end; rooftop amenities open early 2028.
stories.impact: Strong Midtown office leasing signals selective institutional capital recovery in trophy Manhattan locations after years of flight. HQ relocations within the market (Amorepacific) and into renovated buildings (Zeta Global) show tenants investing in placemaking and amenity-rich space, not fleeing. For multifamily developers, this validates continued density and mixed-use demand in Midtown corridor; office-to-residential conversion risk lower than feared in 2023-24.

stories.title: Former Factory to Receive New Life as Affordable Homes in Upstate NY
stories.excerpt: Developers have begun work on a new 80-unit affordable housing property on the site of a former factory in the Adirondack village of Tupper Lake, NY. The $46 million project will transform the long-vacant Oval Wood Dish Factory into modern apartments and more than 25,000 feet of commercial space, with residences affordable to households earning up to 90% of the Area Median Income. Housing Visions, Lahinch Group and Braxton Capital are developing the project, which will be all-electric, utilizing cold-climate heat pump technology for heating and cooling as well as a whole-building ventilation system. The Oval Wood Dish Factory development forms part of Governor Hochul’s $25 billion Housing Plan, which aims to create or preserve 100,000 affordable homes in New York over a five-year period. Oval Wood Dish Factory enjoys a mix of public and private financing, including Federal and State Low-Income Housing Tax Credits (LIHTC) from New York State Homes and Community Renewal (HCR) that are expected to generate more than $17 million in equity. “Under Governor Hochul’s leadership, New York State is making the targeted investments needed to tackle our regional housing shortages head-on,” said Empire State Development President, CEO, & Commissioner Hope Knight in a statement. “The start of construction on the Oval Wood Dish development marks a transformative moment for Tupper Lake and the entire North Country.” The post Former Factory to Receive New Life as Affordable Homes in Upstate NY appeared first on Connect CRE.
bullets: Housing Visions, Lahinch, Braxton Capital developing 80-unit affordable project in Tupper Lake, NY
$46M project, $17M+ LIHTC equity; part of Hochul's $25B Housing Plan (100K units in 5 years)
All-electric cold-climate heat pump tech; long-vacant brownfield-to-residential conversion
stories.summary: Developers have begun work on an 80-unit affordable housing project at the former Oval Wood Dish Factory in Tupper Lake, NY, a small Adirondack village. The $46 million development, funded by LIHTC ($17M+ in equity), Federal and State credits, will serve households up to 90% AMI and include 25,000 SF of commercial space. The project is all-electric with cold-climate heat pump technology.
stories.impact: Limited relevance to multifamily development team focused on market-rate acquisition and value-add. However, signal worth noting: New York State's aggressive affordable housing push (100K units over 5 years) is channeling capital into rural/secondary upstate markets. Tax-exempt financing and LIHTC appetite remain strong even for small-format projects in low-density areas, widening the competitive landscape for acquisition in secondary markets.

stories.title: Colliers Completes Sale of Healthcare Center in Twin Cities Metro
stories.excerpt: Colliers completed the sale of Eagan Medical Center, an outpatient facility located at 1185 Town Centre Drive in Eagan, Minnesota. The sale was led by the Colliers team of Tom O’Brien, Louis Suarez, Jordan Selbiger and Misty Bowe, who represented the seller, Tareen Development Partners (TDP), a Twin Cities-based real estate development firm focused on multifamily, mixed-use and community-driven projects across the Midwest. “TDP’s acquisition of the property in December 2024 marked the beginning of a value-add initiative,” said O’Brien. “By rebranding the former Town Centre Plaza as Eagan Medical Center, completing targeted improvements and driving leasing activity, TDP created a specialty healthcare destination that attracted strong investor interest.” The 43,419-square-foot medical office property is anchored by MNGI Digestive Health, Minnesota Urology and Tareen Dermatology, along with a complementary mix of specialty healthcare providers. Conveniently located near Interstates 35E and 494, the facility offers ample surface and underground parking. The post Colliers Completes Sale of Healthcare Center in Twin Cities Metro appeared first on Connect CRE.
bullets: Tareen Development Partners exited Eagan Medical Center (43.4K SF) via Colliers sale
Value-add medical office play: rebranding, improvements, specialty healthcare anchors (MNGI, Minnesota Urology, dermatology)
Twin Cities market: TDP pivoting medical office; MF/mixed-use focus remains core
stories.summary: Tareen Development Partners (TDP), a Twin Cities-based MF and mixed-use developer, acquired Eagan Medical Center in December 2024, completed value-add improvements, and sold it via Colliers within weeks. The 43,419-SF specialty medical office near I-35E and I-494 was anchored by MNGI Digestive Health, Minnesota Urology, and Tareen Dermatology.
stories.impact: TDP's rapid medical-office flip suggests selective capital discipline and trading out of non-core assets to redeploy into higher-return MF/mixed-use. No direct signal of MF weakness in Twin Cities; rather, evidence of opportunistic tactical exits. Developers should monitor TDP's pipeline for MF activity in Minneapolis-St. Paul; TDP's focus remains residential/mixed-use, not medical office.

stories.title: Essex Realty Group Brokers Sale of 12-Unit MF in Tinley Park
stories.excerpt: Essex Realty Group completed the sale of 17114 71st Avenue, a 12-unit multifamily property in Tinley Park, Illinois, for $1.51 million.The property consists of ten two-bedroom, one-bathroom units and two one-bedroom, one-bathroom units. Two units have been fully renovated, while the remaining ten are in standard condition. The property had been owned by the same seller since 2001 and was acquired by an out-of-state investor with a growing portfolio in the Chicago area. With in-place rents substantially below market, the new owner plans to renovate the remaining units and push rents toward market levels.“This transaction highlights the strong investor appetite we’re seeing for value-add multifamily assets in Chicago’s suburban markets,” said Jimmy Donahue, Director at Essex Realty Group. “With rents well below market, this property gave the buyer a clear roadmap to drive returns, and we were glad to help facilitate a smooth transaction for both parties.” Stay ahead of the multifamily market at Connect Apartments. Gain firsthand insights from industry leaders on capital markets, development, operations, financing, and investment trends while expanding your network with the people making deals happen. See you on September 22! The post Essex Realty Group Brokers Sale of 12-Unit MF in Tinley Park appeared first on Connect CRE.
bullets: Essex Realty brokered 12-unit MF sale in Tinley Park, IL for $1.51M
Property: 10x 2BR/1BA, 2x 1BR/1BA; in-place rents below market; out-of-state buyer
New owner plans full renovation and rent push to market; long-held single-owner property (since 2001)
stories.summary: A 12-unit multifamily property in Tinley Park, Illinois (southwest Chicago suburbs) sold for $1.51 million. The property had been held by the same owner since 2001 and was acquired by an out-of-state investor growing a Chicago-area portfolio. Two units are renovated; the new owner plans to upgrade the remaining ten units and push rents to market.
stories.impact: Classic micro-market MF value-add signal: out-of-state capital entering Chicago suburbs for below-market rent opportunities. Tinley Park reflects suburban Chicago's resilience and accessibility to institutional buyers seeking renovation upside. Indicates sustained demand for 12-50 unit properties in Chicago fringe markets; acquisition pricing and rent arbitrage remain attractive to smaller operators and regional funds despite broader metro supply concerns.

stories.title: Tax-Exempt Commercial Mortgage-Backed Securities Are Having a Moment
stories.excerpt: As the need for affordable housing in the U.S. grows, the tax-exempt commercial mortgage-backed securities (CMBS) market is emerging as a potential financing tool to deliver more homes. New federal rules and greater attention from ratings agencies and top-tier banks are helping the growth of the burgeoning structure. Tax-exempt affordable housing securitizations have taken flight of late after years of largely flying under the radar, according to Ryan Paszczykowski, head of structured investing at Systima Capital Management. Tax-exempt CMBS deals occurred on an occasional basis back in the 2000s, but the structure began to develop consistently in the late 2010s when Citigroup and Freddie Mac rolled out programs offering credit risk transfer securities backed by tax-exempt loans issued by state or local housing agencies. The tax-exempt structures of these deals offer lower costs of capital than standard taxable CMBS or traditional affordable housing loans backed by Fannie Mae or Freddie Mac. Freddie Mac then launched a multifamily loan program in 2017 securitized by tax-exempt loans tied to properties receiving new-issue 4 percent Low-Income Housing Tax Credits (LIHTCs) and expanded its outreach of the offering in late 2024 through a new registration system. Now, the product is starting to take hold as a securitized offering in the municipal debt space at a time when there is increased support nationally to find financial solutions for America’s housing challenges. The deals have become more attractive to investors in a higher interest rate climate since the value of tax-exempt debt stays higher as rates remain elevated while also serving as an attractive option for high-yield investors who are drawn to collateral protections like the federally backed LIHTCs. A recent deal that Systima itself was involved in underscores the increased demand. bullets: Tax-exempt CMBS market emerging as alternative financing for affordable housing
Citigroup, Freddie Mac launched programs in late 2010s; 4% LIHTC securitizations lower cost vs. taxable CMBS
New federal rules and ratings agency attention driving growth in structured affordable housing debt
stories.summary: Tax-exempt commercial mortgage-backed securities (CMBS) are gaining traction as a lower-cost financing vehicle for affordable multifamily development. Citigroup and Freddie Mac pioneered securitization programs backed by tax-exempt loans from state/local housing agencies. Tax-exempt structures offer lower capital costs than standard taxable CMBS or traditional Fannie Mae/Freddie Mac loans, especially for properties with new-issue 4% Low-Income Housing Tax Credits.
stories.impact: Critical for MF developers pursuing affordable/workforce housing: tax-exempt CMBS is opening cheaper debt capital for ground-up and acquisition-plus-rehab projects with LIHTC. Developers should engage with Freddie Mac and Citigroup securitization desks early in underwriting to lock lower rates. This financing tool levels the playing field for smaller/mid-tier operators, potentially increasing competition for MF value-add deals in secondary markets where LIHTC is abundant.

stories.title: Dermatology Chain LaserAway Adds 15th NYC Location on the Upper East Side
stories.excerpt: Skin care, hair removal and body wellness services provider LaserAway is getting ready to open its 15th New York City location on Manhattan’s Upper East Side, Commercial Observer has learned. LaserAway signed a 10-year lease for 1,800 square feet on the ground floor of a mixed-use property at 242 East 86th Street, according to a source close to the deal. Asking rent was $165 per square foot. The Yorkville property is owned by the LLC 244 East 86th Street, which is linked to Shore Assets, according to property records. Michael Miller from The Shopping Center Group represented LaserAway in this deal, while Darrell Rubens and Richard Gelber from Newmark represented the landlord. Rubens and Gelber declined to comment, while Miller did not immediately respond to a request for comment. LaserAway offers clients several services including laser hair removal, Botox injections, cool sculpting, facials, tattoo removal and micro-needling. The company already has an East Side location at 1430 Second Avenue, according to its website. LaserAway’s other New York City locations include 118 Court Street in Brooklyn Heights, 35 East 19th Street in the Flatiron District, and 36-07 30th Avenue in Astoria, Queens. Other outposts are in Morningside Heights, the Meatpacking District, Tribeca and near Lincoln Center. Located on East 86th Street between Second and Third avenues, 242 East 86th Street is a 55,158-square-foot, mid-rise mixed-use property. The building was constructed in 1920 and renovated in 2003, according to Loopnet.com. Amanda Schiavo can be reached at aschiavo@commercialobserver.com.
bullets: LaserAway signed 10-year ground-floor lease, 1,800 SF, Upper East Side Manhattan at $165/SF
15th NYC location; tenant growth in high-density retail; mixed-use property anchored by wellness/services
Demand signal: wellness and experience services thriving in Manhattan urban neighborhoods
stories.summary: Dermatology and wellness chain LaserAway signed a 10-year lease for 1,800 square feet on the ground floor of a mixed-use property at 242 East 86th Street (Upper East Side, Manhattan) at $165 per square foot. This is LaserAway's 15th NYC location, signaling sustained expansion in the metro.
stories.impact: Marginal relevance to MF development unless mixed-use specialist. Signal: ground-floor retail/services tenants are actively seeking ground-floor space in residential neighborhoods (Upper East Side, Yorkville), indicating healthy street-level demand and foot traffic. For mixed-use MF developers, confirms viability of wellness/lifestyle retail in urban neighborhood nodes; tenant quality and lease length (10-year) reflect operator confidence in neighborhood durability.

stories.title: Nuveen Green Capital Closes $173M C-PACE Loan on Miami-Area Condos Project
stories.excerpt: The continued strength of Commercial Property Assessed Clean Energy (C-PACE) debt as a construction financing tool has made a big splash in South Florida. Miami developer Shoma Group has landed a $172.5 million C-PACE loan from Nuveen Green Capital to develop its Shoma Bay mixed-use condominium waterfront project in North Bay Village, Fla., Commercial Observer can first report. This transaction provides further evidence of the power of C-PACE to provide accretive financing for large-scale assets such as Shoma Bay,” Ryan Doyle, senior director of originations, at Nuveen Green Capital, said in a statement. “The project is particularly impactful, as Nuveen Green Capital served as the sole capital provider for this development, which ranks among the five largest C-PACE-financed projects in the state of Florida.” Doyle originated the loan with a Nuveen Green Capital team that also featured Christopher Lawton, head of originations, along with Brendan Moore, director, and Tyler Amano, associate director. One source familiar with the transaction said it’s notable because there’s no other debt provider in the capital stack — just the C-PACE loan, condo sales deposits and equity. Located at 1850 John F. Kennedy Causeway 10 miles northeast of Downtown Miami, the 24-story Shoma Bay development will comprise 333 condo units and retail space anchored by a 36,000-square-foot Publix supermarket. Community amenities will include a rooftop pool deck, a wellness spa, a two-story fitness center, a padel court and coworking spaces. Newmark negotiated the debt with a team consisting of Anthony Orso, Clifford Welden, Daniel Matz and Henry Stimler. “Shoma Bay is an exceptional project that reflects the continued evolution of North Bay Village into one of South Florida’s most dynamic waterfront communities,” Orso said in a statement. Shoma Group did not immediately return a request for comment. Andrew Coen can be reached at acoen@commercialobserver.com.
bullets: Nuveen Green Capital closed $172.5M C-PACE loan for Shoma Bay mixed-use condo project, North Bay Village, FL
Sole capital provider; ranks among top 5 C-PACE-financed projects in Florida
C-PACE as construction financing tool proving accretive for large-scale multifamily/mixed-use waterfront development
stories.summary: Nuveen Green Capital closed a $172.5 million C-PACE (Commercial Property Assessed Clean Energy) loan to Miami-based Shoma Group for Shoma Bay, a mixed-use waterfront condominium project in North Bay Village, Florida. Nuveen served as the sole capital provider, making this one of Florida's five largest C-PACE-financed projects.
stories.impact: C-PACE is maturing as a reliable construction financing tool for waterfront and large mixed-use MF projects in Florida, potentially lowering developer equity requirements and accelerating development timelines. For MF developers in South Florida and coastal metros, C-PACE should be layered into capital stack; sustainability-linked debt (green financing) is increasingly competitive with traditional construction lending, especially for projects >$100M. Monitor C-PACE program expansion in other high-growth states (TX, AZ).

stories.title: Related Ross Buys Land for Major Mixed-Use Dev in Florida
stories.excerpt: Billionaire Stephen Ross has closed on a land acquisition to build a major, open-air mixed-use development in Wellington, a village in Palm Beach County, Fla., renowned for its equestrian scene. Related Ross, the developer’s namesake firm, paid $28.3 million for a 32-acre site at 10400 Stribling Way, just east of State Road 7, property records show. The planned development, called Village Landing, is set to include a 180-room hotel and over 300,000 square feet of retail, office and restaurant space, all connected by six plazas. “Our goal is to create a village center that complements what is already special about Wellington while adding the everyday amenities, restaurants, experiences and connections that are designed to serve the western communities of Palm Beach County,” Kevin Ryan, executive vice president of Related Ross, said in a statement. Starwood Property Trust supplied a $29.1 million loan. Construction is expected to commence in the fall. The western portion of the site, spanning about 44 acres, will be turned into a private grade school, operated by ElevateED. The land sale is expected to close in October, per a representative for Related Ross. The combined 71-acre parcel is part of the Acme Improvement District, which was controlled by the Village of Wellington. In 1953, the Florida Legislature created the special district to manage water drainage and infrastructure development. Village Landing marks Related Ross’ first ground-up development outside of West Palm Beach since launching in 2024 and becoming the city’s biggest office owner. Ross’s goal is to turn West Palm Beach into a leading business hub and attract high-profile tech and finance companies. The West Palm Beach-based firm is building two more office buildings after securing a $772 million construction loan package last year. Two luxury condo developments are under construction. Julia Echikson can be reached at jechikson@commercialobserver.com.
bullets: Related Ross acquired 32-acre site Wellington, FL (Palm Beach County) for $28.3M
Village Landing: 180-room hotel, 300K+ SF retail/office/restaurant, six plazas; Fall 2025 construction start
Equestrian-focused suburban market; western Palm Beach County destination play
stories.summary: Related Ross (Stephen Ross's developer firm) closed acquisition of a 32-acre site in Wellington, Palm Beach County, Florida for $28.3 million. The planned mixed-use development, Village Landing, will include a 180-room hotel, 300,000+ SF of retail, office and restaurant space, and six plazas. Starwood Property Trust provided a $29.1 million construction loan; work is expected to begin fall 2025.
stories.impact: While MF component is not specified in article, Related Ross's $28.3M land acquisition and $29.1M construction financing in Wellington signals suburban Palm Beach County as emerging growth corridor. Wellington's affluence and equestrian brand attract high-income residents; Related Ross's mixed-use placemaking strategy may anchor residential community demand. MF developers should monitor Wellington and western Palm Beach County for follow-on residential projects and competitive entries; Related Ross's anchor project may signal market viability for mid-to-luxury MF in the area.

stories.title: Investor General Atlantic to Anchor Related’s 625 Madison Avenue in 150K-SF Deal
stories.excerpt: Related Companies just nabbed an anchor tenant for its under-construction office tower at 625 Madison Avenue in Manhattan’s Plaza District, the developer announced Tuesday. General Atlantic, a global investment firm, has inked a long-term lease to occupy more than 150,000 square feet across five floors at the planned 53-story office tower, which is slated to open in 2029. The firm will use the space for its more than 330 New York-based employees, who represent about one-third of the company’s global workforce. “General Atlantic has always taken a long-term view, and our new headquarters is an investment in the firm’s future,” Bill Ford, chairman and CEO of General Atlantic, said in a statement. “It will be a place that brings our people and global community together, strengthens the connections that are central to who we are, and gives us room to grow for many decades to come.” The exact length of the lease and the asking rent were not disclosed. The average asking rent for Class A office space in the Plaza District was $97.23 per square foot in the second quarter of 2026, according to Colliers data. Related did not disclose the names of the brokers who worked on this deal. “When we began designing 625 Madison, General Atlantic was exactly the kind of prestigious and ambitious firm we had in mind as an anchor tenant because of the value they place on investment and operational excellence, collaboration and long-term relationships,” Jeff Blau, CEO of Related, said in a statement. “This will be a building of industry leaders, and we are thrilled to have General Atlantic on board and look forward to delivering an exceptional new headquarters for their team.” In tandem with General Atlantic’s lease, private equity firm Veritas Capital has also seemed to secure new office space at 625 Madison Avenue. bullets: General Atlantic leased 150K+ SF across five floors, 625 Madison Avenue, Manhattan (53-story tower, 2029 opening)
Anchor tenant: 330 NYC-based employees (1/3 of global workforce); long-term HQ lease
Flight-to-quality office leasing continues; Plaza District Manhattan market signals institutional confidence in 2029 delivery
stories.summary: Related Companies secured General Atlantic, a global investment firm, as anchor tenant for 625 Madison Avenue, a 53-story office tower under construction in Manhattan's Plaza District (opening 2029). General Atlantic will occupy 150,000+ square feet across five floors as its NYC headquarters for 330 employees. The lease is long-term; rent and term not disclosed.
stories.impact: Institutional capital (General Atlantic, Related) betting heavily on 2029 Manhattan office delivery timing, suggesting conviction that white-collar demand recovery will support trophy office. Long-term HQ lease signals flight-to-quality and consolidation in flagship markets despite hybrid-work trends. For MF developers: Plaza District remains investment-grade market with sustained employment density; expect 625 Madison Avenue's 330-person influx to support residential demand in adjacent neighborhoods (Park Ave South, Murray Hill). Monitor trophy office completions and anchor tenant announces as proxy for CBD residential demand acceleration.
